## 開篇固定收益論點

週五非農就業意外強勁，終結前一交易日有條件的喘息，政策主導的熊市趨平重新成為美國公債的主要格局。非農就業人口增加 172,000 人，優於所有預測，前幾個月數據也向上修正。原先初步顯現的勞動市場降溫，因而轉為市場重新相信名目需求足以承受限制性政策。2 年期殖利率收於 4.17%，10 年期收於 4.55%，前端壓力更大。週四油價下跌及勞動成本訊號轉弱，僅短暫抑制緊縮路徑；非農數據公布後，這條路徑再度開啟。

走勢的組成比名目變動幅度更重要。10 年期實質殖利率升至 2.19%，在損益兩平通膨率持平之下，完全解釋同年期名目殖利率的升幅。面對經濟活動展現韌性及政策利率可能升得更高，投資人要求更高的實質補償，卻未再上調長期通膨補償。最明確的傳導路徑因此是勞動市場韌性推升聯準會政策定價與實質折現率，調整則主要由曲線中段與前端吸收。

跨資產走勢強化這項判斷，也揭露另一個壓力來源。油價下跌，顯示新的能源價格衝擊無法解釋美國公債拋售。科技股反而遭遇劇烈估值修正，美元走強、黃金下跌，波動率大幅攀升。實質殖利率上升直接壓低長存續期間股票的估值，獲利了結、融資疑慮及個別公司消息則進一步放大科技股跌勢。整體走勢反映資金成本重定價，而非傳統的資金轉進政府公債避險。

相較於主要風險資產的劇烈跌勢，融資市場仍具韌性。短天期國庫券殖利率保持平穩；一筆與 Google 相關、已完成的市政債交易在次級市場利差收窄；一項規模極大的晶片融資案也在不同風險層級敲定最終條款。信用基金價格雖然下跌，但實際完成的交易顯示，只要結構清楚界定抵押品、擔保與損失曝險，資金仍可取得。全球政策也形成限制：印度維持利率不變，卻上調通膨預測；歐洲後續討論則讓歐洲央行升息仍是可能選項。因此，前一交易日的核心結論在價格上已有變化，市場格局卻未改變：喘息行情相當脆弱，實質利率底部進一步墊高，但融資管道仍選擇性開放，避免利率衝擊演變成全面性的融資斷裂。

## 美國公債利率、聯準會定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

各指標年期的美國公債殖利率全面上升，且越往長端，債券跌幅越小。2 年期殖利率上升 12 基點至 4.17%，5 年期上升 11 基點至 4.29%，10 年期上升 8 基點至 4.55%，30 年期上升 4 基點至 5.01%。2s10s 利差收窄 4 基點至 38 基點，2s30s 利差收窄 8 基點至 84 基點。這是壓力集中前端的熊市趨平：政策預期及中期實質利率路徑的調整幅度，明顯大於長期通膨補償或財政補償。

曲率顯示壓力集中於曲線前半段，但 5 年期並未特別疲弱。2s5s10s 蝶式利差上升 2 基點至 -14 基點；即使 5 年期債券本身遭到大幅拋售，相較兩翼仍然偏貴。2s10s30s 蝶式利差維持在 -8 基點。全週來看，2 年期與 5 年期殖利率分別上升 19 與 16 基點，10 年期上升 10 基點，30 年期僅上升 2 基點。殖利率曲線反映市場持續重估聯準會政策路徑，而非單日出現長債供給溢價。

抗通膨債券提供最清楚的拆解。5 年期實質殖利率上升 11 基點至 1.81%，7 年期上升 9 基點至 1.99%，10 年期上升 8 基點至 2.19%；20 年期與 30 年期則分別上升 5 與 3 基點，至 2.55% 與 2.74%。10 年期損益兩平通膨率當日維持在 2.36%，也低於此前一週及一個月的水準。名目債券拋售因此反映整體實質折現率結構上移；無論名目公債或抗通膨債券，對衝擊的敏感度都隨年期拉長而下降。

就業報告是主要催化劑，數據廣度也足以推翻週四由勞動市場訊號帶來的喘息。5 月非農就業人口增加 172,000 人，前 2 個月數據向上修正，失業率維持在 4.3%。休閒與餐旅業增加 70,000 個職位，創逾 3 年來最大貢獻；勞動參與率則維持在 61.8%。細項並未顯示招聘動能正快速降溫，幅度也不足以抵銷仍高於目標的通膨。數據公布後，美國公債立即遭到拋售，2 年期殖利率創逾 1 年來最大盤中升幅。

市場將勞動市場韌性轉化為明顯更緊縮的政策路徑。利率交換已完全反映 12 月會議前升息 25 基點，並估計 10 月升息機率約為 60%。市場仍預期 6 月會議按兵不動，但如今聯準會若要保留任何寬鬆傾向，必須提出更充分的理由。新任主席首次主持會議時，面對的將是看似正在回升的勞動市場，以及已受能源與供應干擾推高的通膨。

市場逐漸形成升息共識，不代表政策不確定性已經消失。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁 Beth Hammack 表示，就業接近平衡之際，升息可能很快便屬適當。Citi 仍預期年底前降息 3 次、每次 25 基點，理由是勞動市場將會轉弱。Goldman 則撤除 12 月降息預測，但仍認為升息可能性不高。這些分歧說明了反向力量：一份強勁的非農就業報告足以大幅提高實質利率門檻，但勞動市場強勢能否延續、通膨轉嫁是否持久，仍有待後續數據確認。

美東時間 15:00 公布的消費者信用數據在尾盤增添需求訊號，但並未驅動早盤重定價。4 月借款增加 $207.3億，高於 $178億的市場共識；3 月增幅則修正為 $222.3億。信用總額以年率 4.8% 成長，其中循環信用餘額增加 10.4%，非循環信用增加 2.9%。信用卡借款加速，既可能伴隨消費韌性，也可能反映家庭財務壓力加重。因此，數據更能凸顯名目需求前景的不確定性，尚不足以證明家庭資產負債表轉強。

附息債遭到拋售之際，即期資金狀況仍然有序。4 週、6 週及 8 週期國庫券的附息債等值殖利率均未變動，分別維持在 3.68%、3.68% 與 3.69%；13 週期殖利率也維持在 3.71%。17 週、26 週及 52 週期殖利率則分別上升 2、3 與 5 基點。國庫券殖利率升幅隨年期拉長而擴大，呼應較遠端的政策重定價；最短天期工具則未出現一致性的流動性擾動。

已公告的美國財政部操作構成下一輪市場承接考驗，不能視為週五標售品質的證據。行事曆包括 6 月 8 日標售 $890億的 13 週期國庫券及 $770億的 26 週期國庫券，6 月 9 日接續標售 $650億的 6 週期國庫券及 $500億的 52 週期國庫券。附息債供給包括 $580億的 3 年期新券、$390億的 10 年期增額發行及 $220億的 30 年期增額發行。流動性支持與現金管理買回可改善合格證券的交易，但無法免除投資人承接新增附息債存續期間的需求。

選擇權交易對收盤共識形成有限度的反向訊號。市場出現 7 月到期的 10 年期美國公債買權需求，押注殖利率在涵蓋通膨數據與聯準會會議的期間內降向 4.4%。這項避險顯示，市場也在防範非農數據已將實質殖利率推得過高；若物價數據或政策措辭不如鷹派預期，殖利率可能回落。不過，收盤定價仍要求後續數據必須實際轉弱，才能扭轉走勢。損益兩平通膨率持平、油價下跌及部分經濟學家的不同預測，限制了對拋售的延伸解讀，卻未改變前端與實質殖利率實際主導跌勢的事實。

## 信用、融資與初級市場吸收

信用資產總報酬隨美國公債與股票走弱。LQD 下跌 0.6247%，HYG 下跌 0.5011%，JNK 下跌 0.4368%。投資等級債的存續期間較長，因而表現落後；股市避險情緒升高，也拖累較低信用品質的基金。這些上市基金的報酬顯示估值與風險偏好普遍惡化，但已完成融資案的條款顯示，市場並未關閉，只是准入條件高度分化。

規模約 $10億、與 Alphabet 相關的加州預付能源交易，提供最明確的公開市場承接訊號。California Community Choice Financing Authority 為 Pioneer Community Energy 發行債券，由 Alphabet 擔任金融中介，Goldman Sachs 負責承銷。最大一部分的發行利差較指標高 95 基點。債券其後在次級市場以更窄利差成交，顯示即使政府公債殖利率上升，投資人仍認可其交易結構與交易對手。

市場對 2035 年到期債券的需求尤其明顯。截至週五下午，該券成交金額達 $4.92億，平均利差為 89 基點，部分交易利差更收窄至 74 基點。次級市場表現具有參考價值，因為這是實際完成發行後的交易，而非尚未落實的融資目標。這也顯示，大型科技業交易對手可擴大預付能源債券的投資人基礎，同時為參與交易的公用事業節省長期電力成本。

私募信貸則透過精細分層的結構，承接規模更大的 AI 基礎建設融資需求。Apollo 與 Blackstone 敲定 $350億債務融資，用於購買 Google 設計、再由 Anthropic 透過特殊目的機構承租的晶片。約半數融資已完成分銷。一筆 $60億優先級分層的利差較美國公債高 1 個百分點，另有 $240億優先票據按面額發行，票面利率為 5.75%。兩個層級均取得私募中等投資等級評等，並獲 Broadcom 支持。

損失承擔方式解釋了優先債與次順位債之間的定價差距。$45億的 B 級分層不受 Broadcom 支持，按面額發行，票面利率為 8.5%。若租約違約，出售晶片所得又不足以償還投資人，Broadcom 同意補足優先層級的差額。這項安排將殘值風險移出優先債投資人，使保險公司與銀行能以較低成本為使用年限較長的運算資產提供融資；履約風險則集中於 Anthropic 的租金支付、晶片價值及未受擔保的分層。

週末的投資人評論把已完成的AI融資放進更廣泛的供給與損失嚴重度框架。美國超大型科技公司已在全球發行逾$1,550億無擔保債券，比去年全年高出逾45%；Bloomberg Intelligence則估計，未來5年AI資本支出約達$5兆，其中很大一部分將由債務支應。因此，DoubleLine與Oaktree偏好能承受完整信用循環的結構與資產負債表，並把科技淘汰、資料中心同時開工及最終勝負未明列為主要風險。這項警告並不表示目前債券估值已形成泡沫，而是說明隨著發行擴大，擔保品、保證、到期結構與回收前景將更為重要。

這2筆交易顯示，即使實質殖利率大幅上升，AI融資仍能擴張。市政債投資人接受新的預付能源交易對手，私募信貸機構則區分受擔保的優先債權與直接承擔風險的次順位債權。交易文件清楚界定受償順位與支持機制，因此資金仍然可得。規模本身也涉及存續期間供需：美國公債發行量居高不下之際，科技投資同時占用市政債、私募信貸與保險公司的資產負債表。

收盤後另一項agency市場發展，帶來房貸政策風險。美國總統Donald Trump表示，政府仍在考慮出售Fannie Mae與Freddie Mac持股，但並不急於執行。先前構想是在兩家公司估值約$5,000億以上時出售5%至15%股權，可能籌得約$300億；然而市場對執行產生疑慮後，兩家公司股價年內已下跌逾30%。這項消息未改變週五美國公債收盤，但最終資本結構、政府支持框架及退出託管安排，都可能影響agency融資與房貸利率；部分分析師警告，出售持股可能提高房貸成本。

巴西企業信用市場稍晚的發展，則呈現風險配置的另一端。美國收盤後，Raizen 公布一項庭外協議，涵蓋約 650億雷亞爾、折合 $126億的債務，並獲持有計畫內 75.5% 債務的債權人支持。方案將 45% 債務轉換為股權，其餘 55% 置換為新債。這是企業風險與所有權的移轉，不代表一般再融資管道暢通，也無法解釋週五信用基金的普遍跌勢。

日本週末公布的資料則增添一條發展較慢的再融資傳導管道。截至 3 月止的會計年度，納入統計的日經 225 指數成分企業債務達 ¥678兆，年增 4.6%，主要因收購、投資及股東分配消耗現金。Nippon Steel 為完成 $140億的 United States Steel 收購案，借款增至約原先的 2 倍，並導致 S&P 調降其評等。日本國內利率上升將率先衝擊體質較弱的工業企業；若放款成長持續超過存款，更多借款人可能被迫轉向債券市場，即使利息負擔同步上升。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

日本薪資報告強化日本央行近期正常化的國內條件。實質薪資年增1.9%，高於1.7%的市場預期與上修後前值1.4%；名目薪資則成長3.5%。基本薪資增加3.4%，日本央行關注的全職勞工指標也上升2.6%。實質薪資連續第4個月成長，加上市場普遍預期6月15日至16日會議將升息25個基點，使日本前端利率緊縮更具可信度；不過，中東風險未消之際，薪資漲勢能否持續仍取決於企業獲利與通膨。

印度6月決策維持政策限制性，但沒有立即升息。印度央行一致決議將附買回利率維持在 5.25%，保留中性立場；常設存款機制利率維持在 5.00%，邊際常設融資機制利率與銀行利率則維持在 5.50%。更重要的是，央行將本會計年度通膨預測由 4.6% 上調至 5.1%。對能源進口國而言，利率不變但預期物價路徑上移，將壓縮近期存續期間部位的反彈空間，也加劇全球前端資金競爭。

加拿大是對照美國非農意外最鮮明的已開發市場。5 月就業人口增加 87,800 人，創 2024 年 12 月以來最大增幅，遠高於增加 10,000 人的市場共識；失業率則由 6.9% 降至 6.6%。全職就業及多數產業增聘，推動加拿大 2 年期公債殖利率盤中上升約 10 基點至 2.911%，創 5 月 4 日以來最大升幅；利率交換也反映 12 月前緊縮超過 30 基點。不過，訊號並非單向：就業人口仍較 2025 年底少近 25,000 人，永久全職員工薪資年增率由 4.8% 放緩至 3.2%，低於 4.6%的預期。這份報告挑戰近期經濟萎縮的敘事，卻尚未證明景氣進入持久繁榮。加拿大央行是否將政策利率維持在 2.25%，以及後續政策指引，將檢驗就業反彈能否抵銷薪資放緩與此前職位流失。

台灣 5 月物價數據呈現類似的上游壓力。消費者物價年增率由 1.74% 加速至 2.20%，儘管月增幅縮小。生產者物價年增率由 8.54% 升至 14.11%，美元計價進口物價則上升 17.21%。即使生產者物價月增率放緩，匯率換算效果與進口投入成本仍可能維持國內利率的敏感度。數據擴大亞洲通膨訊號，但尚不足以證明各國政策將同步反應。

歐洲的政策辯論同時面對通膨加速與成長疲弱。歐元區 5 月消費者物價年增率升至 3.2%，週末市場定價傾向歐洲央行在 6 月 11 日會議升息，並反映年底前仍有相當幅度的進一步緊縮。然而，1 年後起算的 1 年期通膨交換已由 4 月高點 2.40% 回落至 2.12%。近期政策定價仍偏鷹派，但中期通膨補償已不如能源衝擊高峰時強烈。

這項分歧使全球利率傳導依年期而異。部分大型資產管理公司預期歐洲央行最多升息 1 次，理由是歐元區經濟活動仍然疲弱，修正後數據也顯示第 1 季產出萎縮。若央行僅採取一次有限的公信力維護行動，壓力可能集中在歐元曲線前端，中期債券仍有反彈空間。若展開連續升息，投資人對各國主權債殖利率曲線要求的相對報酬將提高，歐債也會更直接地與美國公債競爭全球存續期間需求。

財政風險則須與政策利率分開判斷。週五美國市場資料截止後，Morningstar DBRS 將奧地利評等由 AAA 調降至 AA (high)，理由是債務軌跡緩步惡化且財政赤字持續。奧地利政府計畫在 2028 年前將赤字降至 GDP 的 3% 以下，但能源與勞動成本居高不下，持續拖累成長。奧地利 10 年期公債殖利率較相近年期德國公債高 24 基點；市場即時反應有限，顯示此次降評主要確認既有財政疑慮，而非引發新的區域性衝擊。

整體而言，全球存續期間部位並非單一方向的交易。印度雖維持利率不變，卻透過通膨預測傳遞鷹派訊息；台灣上游價格提高國內成本轉嫁風險；歐洲可能緊縮，但反對意見對經濟衰退風險相當敏感；奧地利則增添發行人層級的財政分化。對美國公債而言，共通機制是全球市場出清利率提高，市場也不再深信成長疲弱必然帶來寬鬆。不過，各國實際的成長與通膨結果，仍會限制每一輪緊縮週期的延伸幅度。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場債券在美國收盤時面臨不利環境。EMB 下跌 0.7284%，美元指數上升 0.6639%，同時承受美國公債折現率提高與外幣融資環境收緊的壓力。基金跌勢同時包含存續期間及整體風險效應，不能代表每個主權國家的利差變化。收盤後各國發展顯示，相較於單一市場beta，外部緩衝、財政可信度與負債結構更為重要。塞內加爾提供最明確的短期償付進展。政府在到期日前，提前支付2037年到期歐元債€5,375萬票息，以及2031年到期美元債$3,880萬票息。提前付款降低與IMF談判前的即時違約風險，卻未解決再融資壓力：未來2個月約有7,380億西非法郎國內債務到期，全年計畫籌資約4兆西非法郎；在IMF因先前未揭露借款而取消$18億融資後，期限較短、成本較高的本地發債也正收緊流動性。

哥倫比亞週五稍後公布的通膨數據，強化當地重新緊縮的理由。消費者物價年增率由 5.68% 加速至 5.84%，月增率為 0.47%，一項核心通膨指標則升至 5.79%。結果接近 5.9%的預測中位數，但方向仍然重要。哥倫比亞央行 4 月在決策委員會承受政治壓力之際，意外將政策利率維持在 11.25%；如今核心通膨持續，將提高延長存續期間的成本，也增加央行恢復緊縮的可能性。

較大型新興市場的長端不只承受地緣政治風險。自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，南韓、巴西、南非與墨西哥公債殖利率均上升逾 40 基點。通膨預期解釋大部分升幅，但政府補貼燃料與食品，使預算壓力加重，實質殖利率也隨之上升。若和平協議促使油價下跌，曲線前端可迅速受惠；長天期債券仍須消化國防支出、能源韌性投資、AI 資本需求及財政狀況轉弱。

巴西與南韓呈現不同形式的長端僵固性。巴西指標殖利率維持在 14% 以上，公共債務總額超過 GDP 的 80%，經濟成長仍然穩健。南韓 10 年期公債殖利率則徘徊在 4.25%，接近 2 年高點，追加預算發債又加重通膨壓力及半導體帶動的需求。因此，即使能源價格回落，兩國長存續期間資產的表現仍取決於財政供給與實質利率補償。

印尼週末的干預凸顯更迫切的信心問題。印尼盾今年以來已貶值約 8%，並跌破 1 美元兌 18,000 印尼盾，外國投資人則自債市淨撤出 $4.22億。主管機關進場支撐市場，使 10 年期公債跌幅受到控制，並承諾提供更多流動性。印尼央行也提議提高政府存放於央行的存款利率，希望抵銷部分主權債利息負擔增幅。

印尼措施能否支撐公債價格與政府現金流，取決於規模、計息方式及對發債的影響是否清楚。能源補貼增加已使預算承壓，若相關條款仍不明確，可能進一步模糊財政與貨幣政策的責任界線。哥倫比亞與印尼的對比值得注意：前者面對通膨再度升溫，以及政治力量對政策反應函數施壓；後者則面對匯率疲弱及協調干預引發的公信力疑慮。兩者最終都透過投資人要求更高風險溢價，傳導至存續期間部位。

中國加強查核海外投資，為民間流動性帶來另一項限制。稅務機關向高資產居民追繳最高20%的投資收益稅，並可能加收逾期罰款；中信證券估計，香港可能有多達HK$2,500億資產受到影響。前一年居民資金外流估計創下$8,070億紀錄。強化執法可以把資本留在境內並支持國際收支，卻也可能促使投資組合匯回、降低離岸風險偏好，並擴大官方外匯存底總額與民間可自由運用流動性之間的差距。

中國5月底外匯存底數據提供部分區域緩衝。官方外匯存底增加 $317億至 $3.4422兆，月增 0.93%。外匯主管機關表示，變化主要來自匯率換算及全球資產價格波動，因此不能直接將增幅解讀為干預規模或資本流入。不過，中國仍握有龐大的外匯存底總額，可用來緩和外部波動；其流動性條件因此有別於正面臨迫切再融資或政策公信力壓力的主權國家。

## 跨資產

油價走勢不支持以通膨衝擊解釋週五利率上升。WTI 下跌 2.687% 至 $90.54，Brent 下跌 2.0415% 至 $93.09。兩者全週仍然上漲，表示較廣泛的能源成本轉嫁風險尚未消失；但油價單日回落，恰逢 10 年期損益兩平通膨率持平、實質殖利率大幅上升。推動美國公債拋售的主要力量是非農就業與政策定價，而非原油再度飆升。

股票市場劇烈反映折現率上升。S&P 500 下跌 2.6445%，Nasdaq 100 下跌 4.7692%，半導體指數重挫 10.257%；VIX 則大漲 39.6753% 至 21.51。長存續期間科技股的估值對實質殖利率上升最為敏感，市場對 AI 投資規模及融資方式的疑慮又進一步加深跌勢。

股市拋售並非純粹由總體因素造成。科技股在週五前已快速上漲，累積相當大的獲利了結空間；Broadcom 展望不如預期、Meta 可能進行股權融資、比特幣走弱，以及投資人為大型發行籌措現金，也都增添賣壓。投資人同時轉向防禦型產業，S&P 500 仍有 5 個類股上漲。這些細節顯示利率並非股市下跌的唯一原因，但未推翻兩者共同受到估值調整影響的傳導機制。

美元與黃金也印證實質利率上升的方向。美國相對政策預期轉趨緊縮，美元指數升至 100.07；黃金期貨則下跌 3.0989% 至 $4,337.10。股市下跌期間，黃金未能發揮傳統避險功能，原因是美元走強及實質殖利率上升，提高了持有黃金的機會成本。這種環境收緊外部借款人的融資條件，也加重新興市場債券基金跌勢。

週末的政策與地緣政治消息，界定下一次開盤的風險，但不能倒寫為週五價格成因。聯準會理事Michael Barr警告，降低銀行資本、流動性與監管要求，可能讓脆弱性逐步累積並最終損害放款能力，直接反駁監管副主席Michelle Bowman主導的鬆綁方向。歐洲方面，Volodymyr Zelenskyy提出全面停火及直接和平談判，但Vladimir Putin在英、法、德領袖準備會晤Zelenskyy前拒絕見面。這次接觸未能展開，限制烏克蘭風險溢酬近期下降的可能性；油市則仍更聚焦另一條美國與伊朗局勢的傳導路徑。

信用基金、股票與黃金同步下跌，美國公債也遭到賣出，使美元成為唯一明確的避險受益者。最短天期國庫券未受干擾，加上多筆融資順利完成，顯示市場並未發生全面性的現金緊縮。跨資產走勢反映的是有序但劇烈的折現率重定價，並受到擁擠的科技股部位及地緣政治不確定性放大。油價下跌仍是最重要的反向力量；若能源價格持續回落，維持限制性政策的通膨理由可能隨之減弱。

## 前瞻市場意義

6 月 10 日美東時間 08:30 公布的 5 月美國 CPI，以及 6 月 11 日同一時間公布的 PPI 與初次申領失業救濟金人數，將決定週五由實質殖利率主導的熊市趨平能否延續。市場共識預期整體 CPI 月增 0.5%、年增 4.2%，前值分別為 0.6% 與 3.8%；核心 CPI 月增率則預期由 0.4% 放緩至 0.3%。若核心項目普遍強勁，且隨後公布的 PPI 接近或高於整體月增 0.6%、核心月增 0.5%的預期，將支持市場對年底前升息的定價，使 2 年期、5 年期及 10 年期實質殖利率持續承受上行壓力。若基礎通膨轉弱，初次申領失業救濟金人數又高於前值 225,000 人，則會挑戰「非農就業轉強必然要求更高政策利率路徑」的推論，並可能重啟週五中止的存續期間反彈。

6 月 8 日至 11 日的美國公債供給，將檢驗穩定的現金市場能否承接年期更重的發行組合。首批標售為 $890億的 13 週期及 $770億的 26 週期國庫券，隨後還有 $650億的 6 週期國庫券、$500億的 52 週期國庫券、$580億的 3 年期新券、$390億的 10 年期增額發行，以及 $220億的 30 年期增額發行。應觀察標售出清水準相對於當時次級市場的表現、投標倍數、各類投標者獲配比例、交易商承接比例，以及交割前後的國庫券殖利率。若需求廣泛、現金利率維持有序，將確認週五走勢屬於總體與實質利率重定價，市場資產負債表仍有承接能力。若附息債需求疲弱、交易商庫存增加或交割出現壓力，供給便可能重新成為獨立的殖利率曲線驅動因素，其中 10 年期、30 年期及利率敏感型企業發債承受的壓力最大。

全球政策觀察依序包括 6 月 10 日公布的中國 5 月通膨數據、當日稍晚的加拿大央行決策、6 月 11 日的歐洲央行決策，以及 6 月 12 日的印度 CPI。中國整體消費者物價與出廠價格相對於年增 1.4% 及 3.5%的預期，將影響亞洲存續期間資產；加拿大是否將政策利率維持在 2.25%，以及歐洲央行是否如預期升息 25 基點，則會顯示能源進口國央行如何權衡通膨與成長轉弱。若歐洲央行訊號僅限於一次升息、中國上游價格壓力受控，且印度通膨接近或低於 4.00%的市場共識，將削弱全球同步緊縮的論點。若物價普遍加速，或政策指引指向連續升息，則會確認全球市場出清利率進一步走高，使歐洲曲線前端、亞洲貨幣、新興市場長天期殖利率及美國公債期限結構持續承壓。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Friday’s payroll surprise ended the prior close’s conditional relief and restored a policy-led bear flattening as the dominant Treasury regime. Nonfarm payrolls increased 172,000, topping every forecast, and prior months were revised higher. The result converted tentative labor cooling into renewed confidence that nominal demand can tolerate restrictive policy. The 2-year yield closed at 4.17% and the 10-year at 4.55%, with the front end under the greater pressure. That pattern reopened the tightening path that Thursday’s lower oil and softer labor-cost signals had only temporarily restrained.

The composition was more important than the size of the nominal move. The 10-year real yield rose to 2.19%, accounting for the full increase in the corresponding nominal yield because breakeven inflation was unchanged. Investors demanded more real compensation for resilient activity and a potentially higher policy rate; they did not mark up long-horizon inflation compensation again. The strongest causal channel therefore ran from labor resilience into Federal Reserve pricing and real discount rates, with the belly and front end absorbing most of the adjustment.

Cross assets reinforced that interpretation while revealing a second source of stress. Oil declined, so a fresh energy-price shock could not explain the Treasury selloff. Technology shares instead suffered a sharp valuation reset, the dollar strengthened, gold fell and volatility jumped. Higher real yields were transmitted directly into long-duration equity valuations, though profit-taking, financing concerns and company news amplified the technology move. The combination looked like a repricing of the cost of capital, not a conventional flight toward government bonds.

Funding markets remained more resilient than headline risk assets. Short bill yields were calm, a completed Google-linked municipal transaction tightened in secondary trading, and a very large chip-financing package reached final terms across several layers of risk. Credit-fund prices fell, yet completed deals showed that capital was still available when structures allocated collateral, guarantees and loss exposure clearly. Global policy evidence added another constraint: India held rates while raising its inflation forecast, and later European debate kept an ECB increase in view. The central conclusion from the prior session has therefore changed in price but not in regime: relief proved fragile, the real-rate floor strengthened, and selective financing access prevented a rates shock from becoming a generalized funding break.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Treasury yields rose across every benchmark maturity, with losses diminishing toward the long end. The 2-year increased 12 basis points to 4.17%, the 5-year added 11 to 4.29%, the 10-year rose 8 to 4.55%, and the 30-year climbed 4 to 5.01%. The 2s10s slope narrowed 4 basis points to 38, while 2s30s flattened 8 to 84. This was a front-loaded bear flattening: policy expectations and the medium-term real-rate path moved more abruptly than long-run inflation or fiscal compensation.

Curvature located the pressure in the front half without making the 5-year sector uniquely weak. The 2s5s10s butterfly rose 2 basis points to -14, leaving the 5-year relatively rich to its wings even after its large outright selloff. The 2s10s30s butterfly held at -8. Over the week, 2- and 5-year yields had risen 19 and 16 basis points, against 10 at 10 years and only two at 30 years. The curve was carrying a cumulative reassessment of the Fed path, not a 1-day long-bond supply premium.

Inflation-linked securities gave the cleanest decomposition. The 5-year real yield rose 11 basis points to 1.81%, the 7-year increased 9 to 1.99%, and the 10-year added 8 to 2.19%. The 20- and 30-year real yields rose 5 and 3 basis points, to 2.55% and 2.74%. 10-year breakeven inflation stayed at 2.36% on the day and was lower over the preceding week and month. The nominal selloff therefore reflected a higher real discount-rate structure, with the same declining sensitivity by maturity visible in both nominal and inflation-protected bonds.

The employment report supplied the catalyst and enough breadth to overturn Thursday’s labor relief. Payrolls increased 172,000 in May after upward revisions to the prior 2 months, and the unemployment rate held at 4.3%. Leisure and hospitality added 70,000 positions, its strongest contribution in more than 3 years, while labor-force participation stayed at 61.8%. The details did not show an economy losing hiring momentum quickly enough to offset above-target inflation. Treasuries sold off immediately after the release, and the 2-year’s intraday rise was the largest in more than a year.

Market pricing translated that resilience into a substantially firmer policy path. Interest-rate swaps fully embedded a quarter-point increase by the December meeting and assigned roughly a 60% chance to an October move. The June meeting remained associated with a hold, but the burden shifted toward the Fed explaining why policy should retain any easing bias. The new chairman’s 1st meeting now sits between a labor market that appears to be recovering and inflation already elevated by energy and supply disruptions.

Policy uncertainty did not disappear simply because the market converged on a hike. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said an increase may soon be appropriate with employment near balance. Citi continued to expect 3 quarter-point reductions late in the year, arguing that labor would soften, while Goldman removed its December cut forecast yet still regarded an increase as unlikely. Those disagreements identify the counterforce: 1 strong payroll report can raise the real-rate hurdle decisively, but the persistence of labor strength and inflation pass-through still has to be established.

The 15:00 ET consumer-credit release added a late demand signal without driving the morning repricing. April borrowing increased by $20.73 billion, above the $17.80 billion consensus and after a revised $22.23 billion March gain. Total credit grew at a 4.8% annual rate, with revolving balances up 10.4% and nonrevolving credit up 2.9%. Faster card borrowing can accompany resilient consumption or greater household strain, so it reinforces nominal-demand uncertainty more clearly than it establishes stronger household balance sheets.

Immediate cash conditions remained orderly beneath the coupon selloff. 4-, 6- and 8-week coupon-equivalent bill yields were unchanged at 3.68%, 3.68% and 3.69%. The 13-week yield also held at 3.71%, while 17-week, 26-week and 52-week yields rose 2, 3 and 5 basis points. The adjustment increased with maturity across bills, mirroring policy repricing farther out, while the shortest instruments showed no common liquidity disturbance.

Announced Treasury operations now create the next absorption sequence, not evidence about auction quality on Friday. The calendar contains $89 billion of 13-week bills and $77 billion of 26-week bills on June 8, followed by $65 billion of 6-week and $50 billion of 52-week bills on June 9. Coupon supply comprises $58 billion at 3 years, a $39 billion 10-year reopening and a $22 billion 30-year reopening. Liquidity-support and cash-management buybacks can improve trading in eligible securities, but they do not remove the need for investors to absorb the new coupon duration.

Options activity supplied a limited challenge to the closing consensus. Demand appeared for July 10-year calls targeting a yield decline toward 4.4% over a period spanning inflation data and the Fed meeting. That hedge is consistent with a market aware that payrolls may have pushed real yields too far if price data or policy language disappoint hawkish expectations. The close nonetheless placed the burden on softer evidence: flat breakevens, declining oil and alternative economist forecasts restrained the selloff’s interpretation, but none displaced its observed front-end and real-yield leadership.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Credit total returns weakened alongside Treasuries and equities. LQD fell 0.6247%, HYG declined 0.5011%, and JNK lost 0.4368%. The larger duration exposure of investment grade contributed to its underperformance, while the risk-off equity session weighed across lower-quality funds. These listed returns describe a broad deterioration in valuation and risk tone; completed financing terms show that access remained open and highly selective.

The roughly $1 billion California prepaid-energy transaction linked to Alphabet offered the clearest public-market absorption signal. California Community Choice Financing Authority issued the bonds for Pioneer Community Energy, with Alphabet serving as the financial intermediary and Goldman Sachs underwriting. The largest portion priced 95 basis points above its benchmark. It subsequently changed hands at tighter levels, indicating that investors found the structure and counterparty attractive even as government yields rose.

Demand was particularly visible in the 2035 maturity. Trading in that security reached $492 million by Friday afternoon, at an average spread of 89 basis points and with some transactions as tight as 74. The secondary performance matters because it followed an actual completed sale, unlike an announced financing target. It also shows how a major technology counterparty can broaden the prepaid-energy buyer base while delivering long-term electricity savings to the participating utility.

Private credit absorbed a much larger AI infrastructure requirement through a carefully tiered structure. Apollo and Blackstone finalized $35 billion of debt to finance Google-designed chips that Anthropic will lease through a special-purpose vehicle. About half of the package was syndicated. A $6 billion senior tranche priced 1 percentage point over Treasuries, and $24 billion of additional senior notes priced at par with a 5.75% coupon. Both layers carried private mid-investment-grade ratings and support from Broadcom.

Loss allocation explained the gap to the junior debt. The $4.5 billion B tranche had no Broadcom backing and priced at par with an 8.5% coupon. For the senior layers, Broadcom agreed to cover any shortfall if a defaulted lease led to chip sales that failed to repay investors. The structure transferred residual-value risk away from senior buyers, allowing insurers and banks to fund long-lived computing assets at a lower cost. It also concentrated performance risk in Anthropic’s lease payments, chip values and the unguaranteed tranche.

Weekend investor commentary put the completed AI financing into a broader supply and loss-severity frame. US hyperscalers had already sold more than $155 billion of unsecured bonds globally, over 45% more than their entire prior-year issuance, while Bloomberg Intelligence estimated roughly $5 trillion of AI capital expenditure over the next 5 years, much of it debt-funded. DoubleLine and Oaktree were therefore favoring structures and balance sheets able to survive a deep cycle, citing technology obsolescence, simultaneous data-center construction and uncertain eventual winners. The warning did not imply that current bond valuations were already a bubble; it explained why collateral, guarantees, maturity and recovery prospects mattered more as issuance scaled.

The 2 transactions show why AI financing can expand even during a real-yield shock. Municipal investors accepted a new prepaid-energy counterparty, while private lenders differentiated between guaranteed senior claims and exposed junior claims. Capital remained available because documentation specified the payment waterfall and support mechanism. The scale is also a duration consideration: technology investment is drawing on municipal, private-credit and insurance balance sheets at the same time that Treasury issuance remains heavy.

A separate after-close agency development introduced a mortgage-market policy risk. President Donald Trump said a Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac share sale remained under consideration but was not urgent. Earlier proposals contemplated selling 5% to 15% of the enterprises at a valuation of about $500 billion or more, potentially raising around $30 billion, while their shares had fallen more than 30% during the year as execution doubts grew. The announcement did not alter Friday's Treasury close, but the eventual capitalization, government-support framework and release from conservatorship could affect agency funding and mortgage rates; some analysts warned that a sale could raise borrowing costs.

A later development in Brazilian corporate credit showed the other end of that allocation process. After the US close, Raizen disclosed an out-of-court agreement covering about 65 billion reais, or $12.6 billion, of debt, supported by creditors holding 75.5% of the obligations in the plan. The proposal converts 45% into equity and exchanges the remaining 55% for new debt. This is a transfer of enterprise risk and ownership, not evidence of routine refinancing access, and it did not explain Friday’s broad fund moves.

Weekend evidence from Japan added a slower-moving refinancing channel. Debt among reporting Nikkei 225 companies reached ¥678 trillion for the fiscal year through March, 4.6% more than a year earlier, as acquisitions, investment and shareholder distributions consumed cash. Nippon Steel’s borrowing doubled around its $14 billion acquisition of United States Steel, contributing to an S&P downgrade. Rising domestic rates will hit weaker industrial credits first, and loan growth that outruns deposits can push more borrowers toward bond markets even as their interest burden rises.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Japan's wage report strengthened the domestic case for near-term BOJ normalization. Inflation-adjusted pay rose 1.9% from a year earlier, above the 1.7% consensus and a revised 1.4% prior gain, while nominal wages increased 3.5%. Base pay rose 3.4%, and the full-time-worker measure monitored by the BOJ advanced 2.6%. With real wages rising for a 4th month and the June 15-16 meeting widely expected to deliver a quarter-point increase, the data made Japanese front-end tightening more credible, although the durability of wage gains still depended on profits and inflation amid Middle East risk.

India’s June decision preserved policy restraint without adding an immediate rate increase. The Reserve Bank of India unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25%, retained a neutral stance and kept the standing deposit facility at 5.00%, with the marginal standing facility and Bank Rate at 5.50%. More consequentially, it raised its fiscal-year inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%. An unchanged rate accompanied by a higher price path limits the scope for near-term duration relief in an energy-importing economy and reinforces competition for global front-end capital.

Canada supplied the clearest developed-market labor counterpoint to the US payroll surprise. Employment rose 87,800 in May, the largest gain since December 2024 and far above the 10,000 consensus, while unemployment fell to 6.6% from 6.9%. Full-time hiring and broad industry gains pushed the 2-year Canadian yield about 10 basis points higher to 2.911%, its largest intraday rise since May 4, and swaps priced more than 30 basis points of tightening by December. The signal was not one-sided: employment remained almost 25,000 below end-2025, and permanent full-time wage growth slowed to 3.2% from 4.8%, below the 4.6% expectation. The report challenged the recent contraction narrative without proving a durable boom, making the Bank of Canada’s 2.25% hold and coming guidance a test of whether the rebound outweighed softer wages and prior job losses.

Taiwan’s May price data showed a related pipeline problem. Consumer inflation accelerated to 2.20% year on year from 1.74%, despite a smaller monthly increase. Producer prices were 14.11% higher than a year earlier, up from 8.54%, and US-dollar import prices rose 17.21%. Currency translation and imported inputs can sustain local rate sensitivity even when monthly producer prices soften. The release broadens the Asian inflation signal without establishing a synchronized policy response.

Europe’s debate combined faster inflation with a weak growth counterweight. Euro-area consumer inflation reached 3.2% in May, and weekend pricing favored an ECB increase at the June 11 meeting with substantial additional tightening embedded through year-end. The 1-year, 1-year inflation swap had retreated to 2.12% from an April peak of 2.40%, however. Near-term policy pricing remained hawkish, while medium-term compensation no longer showed the same intensity as at the height of the energy shock.

That divergence creates a maturity-specific global transmission. Some large asset managers expected 1 ECB increase at most because euro-area activity remained weak, and revised data showed Q1 output contracting. A limited credibility move could keep pressure concentrated at the euro front end and leave room for intermediate bonds to recover. A sequence of increases would raise the relative return needed across sovereign curves and compete more directly with Treasuries for global duration demand.

Fiscal risk remained separate from the policy-rate argument. After Friday’s US cutoff, Morningstar DBRS lowered Austria to AA (high) from AAA, citing a slowly worsening debt trajectory and persistent deficits. The government aims to bring the deficit below 3% of GDP by 2028, while elevated energy and labor costs weigh on growth. Austria’s 10-year bonds yielded 24 basis points more than comparable German debt, and the limited immediate reaction suggested the downgrade formalized an existing fiscal concern more than it created a new regional shock.

Together, these developments keep global duration from moving as a single trade. India’s hold carried hawkish information through the forecast, Taiwan’s pipeline prices raised local pass-through risk, and Europe paired prospective tightening with recession-sensitive dissent. Austria added issuer-specific fiscal differentiation. For Treasuries, the common mechanism is a higher global clearing rate and less confidence that weak growth automatically produces easing, even though country-level growth and inflation outcomes still constrain how far each tightening cycle can extend.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt faced a difficult US close. EMB declined 0.7284% as the dollar index rose 0.6639%, combining higher Treasury discount rates with a tighter external-currency backdrop. The fund move included duration and broad risk effects and does not describe every sovereign spread. Country developments after the close showed why external buffers, fiscal credibility and liability structure matter more than a single beta measure. Senegal supplied the clearest near-term payment delta. The government paid a €53.75 million coupon on its 2037 euro bond and $38.8 million on its 2031 dollar notes before both were due the following week. Early payment reduced immediate default risk ahead of IMF talks, but it did not resolve refinancing pressure: about 738 billion CFA francs of domestic debt service was due over the next 2 months, planned annual borrowing was around 4 trillion CFA francs, and shorter, higher-cost local issuance was tightening liquidity after the IMF canceled a $1.8 billion facility over previously undisclosed borrowing.

Colombia’s inflation release later on Friday strengthened the local tightening case. Annual consumer inflation accelerated to 5.84% from 5.68%, monthly prices rose 0.47%, and a core measure reached 5.79%. The result was close to the 5.9% median forecast, yet the direction matters after the central bank unexpectedly held its rate at 11.25% in April amid political pressure on the board. Persistent core inflation raises the cost of extending duration and increases the chance that policy tightening returns.

Across larger emerging markets, the long end carries more than geopolitical risk. Yields in South Korea, Brazil, South Africa and Mexico had climbed more than 40 basis points since the Iran war began. Inflation expectations explained much of the rise, but real yields also increased as fiscal support for fuel and food strained budgets. Lower oil after a peace agreement could benefit front ends quickly; long maturities would still have to absorb defense spending, energy-resilience investment, AI capital requirements and weaker fiscal positions.

Brazil and South Korea illustrate distinct forms of that inertia. Brazilian benchmark yields remained above 14% as gross public debt exceeded 80% of GDP and growth stayed firm. Korea’s 10-year yield hovered near a 2-year high of 4.25%, with supplementary-budget issuance adding to inflation and semiconductor-led demand. Both cases make long-duration performance dependent on fiscal supply and real-rate compensation, even if energy prices retreat.

Indonesia’s weekend intervention exposed a more immediate confidence problem. The rupiah had fallen about 8% during the year and breached 18,000 per dollar, while foreign investors had withdrawn a net $422 million from bonds. Authorities supported the market sufficiently to limit the decline in 10-year debt and pledged more liquidity. Bank Indonesia also proposed paying a higher rate on government deposits held at the central bank, aiming to offset some of the sovereign’s rising interest burden.

The Indonesian measure can support yields and government cash flow only if its scale, remuneration and issuance effects are clear. Uncertainty about those terms risks blurring fiscal and monetary responsibilities when higher energy subsidies are already straining the budget. The contrast with Colombia is instructive: 1 market faces renewed inflation and political pressure on the reaction function; the other faces currency weakness and credibility questions around coordinated intervention. Both transmit into duration through a higher required risk premium.

China's enforcement against offshore investment added a private-sector liquidity qualification. Tax authorities were pursuing wealthy residents for levies of as much as 20% on investment gains plus possible late-payment penalties, and Citic Securities estimated that as much as HK$250 billion of Hong Kong assets could be affected. The measure followed estimated resident outflows of a record $807 billion in the prior year. Stronger enforcement can retain domestic capital and support the balance of payments, but it can also prompt portfolio repatriation, reduce offshore risk appetite and widen the gap between gross official reserves and freely deployable private liquidity.

China’s end-May reserve data supplied a partial regional buffer. Official foreign-exchange reserves rose by $31.7 billion to $3.4422 trillion, a 0.93% monthly increase. The foreign-exchange authority attributed the change mainly to currency conversion and global asset-price movements, so the increase should not be treated as a direct measure of intervention or capital inflow. It nevertheless leaves a large gross reserve stock available to moderate external volatility, distinguishing China’s liquidity position from sovereigns facing immediate refinancing or policy-credibility stress.

## Cross asset

Oil challenged an inflation-led explanation for Friday’s rates move. WTI fell 2.687% to $90.54 and Brent declined 2.0415% to $93.09. Both remained higher over the week, preserving the broader energy-pass-through risk, yet their daily retreat coincided with flat 10-year breakevens and sharply higher real yields. Payrolls and policy pricing, not a renewed crude spike, supplied the dominant Treasury impulse.

Equities transmitted the higher discount rate with exceptional force. The S&P 500 dropped 2.6445%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 4.7692%, and the semiconductor index fell 10.257%. The VIX jumped 39.6753% to 21.51. Long-duration technology valuations were most exposed to the real-yield rise, and concern over the scale and financing of AI investment deepened the adjustment.

The equity selloff was not a pure macro reaction. Technology shares had risen rapidly before Friday, creating room for profit-taking, and a disappointing Broadcom outlook, possible equity financing by Meta, bitcoin weakness and cash raising ahead of large offerings added pressure. Five of the S&P 500’s sectors still advanced as investors rotated toward defensive industries. Those details qualify the link between rates and stocks without erasing the common valuation channel.

The dollar and gold confirmed the real-rate direction. The dollar index gained to 100.07 as relative US policy expectations firmed, while gold futures fell 3.0989% to $4,337.10. Gold failed to provide conventional protection during the equity decline because the stronger dollar and higher real yields raised its opportunity cost. This combination tightened conditions for external borrowers and reinforced the EM fund loss.

Weekend policy and geopolitical news identified risks for the next open without rewriting Friday's price action. Fed Governor Michael Barr warned that weaker bank capital, liquidity and supervision could allow vulnerabilities to build and eventually impair lending, directly challenging the deregulatory direction under Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman. In Europe, Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered a full ceasefire and direct peace talks, but Vladimir Putin rejected a meeting before UK, French and German leaders prepared to meet Zelenskyy. The failed opening limited immediate prospects for a Ukraine risk-premium reduction even as oil markets remained more focused on the separate US-Iran channel.

Credit funds, equities and gold all weakened while Treasuries also sold off, leaving no clean haven beneficiary beyond the dollar. The absence of a shortest-bill disturbance and the successful financing cases argue against a generalized cash seizure. Cross assets instead describe an orderly but severe repricing of discount rates, amplified by crowded technology exposure and geopolitical uncertainty. Falling oil is the central unresolved counterforce because sustained relief there could weaken the inflation rationale for keeping policy restrictive.

## Forward Market Significance

The May US CPI release at 08:30 ET on June 10, followed by PPI and initial claims at 08:30 ET on June 11, will determine whether Friday’s real-yield-led flattening can persist. Consensus expects headline CPI to rise 0.5% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier, after 0.6% and 3.8%, with core monthly inflation slowing to 0.3% from 0.4%. Broad strength across core components, followed by producer prices near or above the expected 0.6% headline and 0.5% core monthly increases, would validate the market’s year-end hike pricing and keep 2-, 5- and 10-year real yields under upward pressure. Softer underlying inflation alongside a rise in claims from the prior 225,000 would challenge the inference that stronger payrolls require a higher policy path and could reopen the duration relief that ended on Friday.

Treasury supply between June 8 and June 11 will show whether stable cash conditions extend into a heavier maturity mix. The $89 billion 13-week and $77 billion 26-week bill auctions begin the sequence, followed by $65 billion at 6 weeks, $50 billion at 52 weeks, a $58 billion 3-year new issue, a $39 billion 10-year reopening and a $22 billion 30-year reopening. The observable signals are clearing levels against contemporaneous trading, bid-to-cover, bidder allocations, dealer retention and the behavior of bill yields around settlement. Broad demand and orderly cash rates would confirm that Friday was a macro and real-rate repricing with intact balance-sheet capacity. Weak coupon demand, rising dealer inventories or settlement pressure would reopen supply as an independent curve driver, with the 10- and 30-year sectors and rate-sensitive corporate issuance most exposed.

The global sequence centers on China’s May inflation data on June 10, the Bank of Canada decision later that day, the ECB decision on June 11 and India’s CPI release on June 12. China’s headline and factory-gate results relative to expectations of 1.4% and 3.5% year-on-year inflation will shape Asian duration, while a Canadian hold at 2.25% and the ECB’s choice around an expected quarter-point increase will reveal how energy-importing central banks balance inflation against weaker growth. An ECB signal limited to 1 move, contained Chinese pipeline pressure and Indian inflation near or below the 4.00% consensus would challenge the idea of a synchronized tightening cycle. Broader price acceleration or guidance pointing to repeated increases would confirm a higher global clearing rate, keeping European front ends, Asian currencies, long EM yields and the Treasury term structure under pressure.

section_summaries.market_read: The close re-established a policy-led, real-rate bear flattening without a cash-market rupture.

section_summaries.summary: Payroll strength overturned the prior session’s tentative relief, lifting real yields and concentrating Treasury losses in the front end. Falling oil and unchanged long-run inflation compensation pointed to a higher policy and discount-rate path, while orderly bills and completed financings kept the shock from becoming a broad funding break.

section_summaries.market_read: Front-end and belly sensitivity now dominate the Treasury regime, with inflation persistence decisive.
section_summaries.next_check: Watch whether core inflation breadth sustains year-end hike pricing and upward real-yield pressure.
section_summaries.section_title: UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure
section_summaries.summary: Losses declined with maturity as stronger hiring pushed the market toward a firmer Fed path, while real yields rose and long-run breakevens held steady. The curve therefore reflected front-loaded policy repricing rather than a distinct long-bond supply shock, although upcoming auctions will test absorption.

section_summaries.market_read: Credit weakness reflected duration and risk repricing, not a wholesale closure of financing access.
section_summaries.next_check: Watch whether new deals clear without greater concessions as Treasury supply absorbs balance sheet.
section_summaries.summary: Credit funds weakened with Treasuries and equities, but completed municipal and private deals showed financing remained available when collateral, guarantees, and loss allocation were explicit. That selectivity insulated funding from the broader real-yield shock, while exposed junior claims and indebted issuers retained refinancing risk.

section_summaries.market_read: Canada’s jobs rebound extended the US labor shock into another developed-market front end.
section_summaries.next_check: The Bank of Canada must weigh stronger hiring against slower wages and earlier contraction.
section_summaries.section_title: Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission
section_summaries.summary: Canada added 87,800 jobs and its 2-year yield jumped about 10 basis points, challenging the prior contraction narrative even as wage growth slowed. India’s higher inflation forecast, Taiwan’s pipeline prices and Europe’s hawkish debate kept global front-end pressure elevated, while Austria added fiscal differentiation.

section_summaries.market_read: External funding conditions tightened, increasing differentiation by policy credibility and buffers.
section_summaries.next_check: Watch whether currency support and clearer fiscal terms stabilize Indonesia’s sovereign duration.
section_summaries.section_title: EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk
section_summaries.summary: Emerging-market debt faced simultaneous pressure from higher Treasury real yields and a stronger dollar, but country outcomes depended on inflation, fiscal supply, currency buffers, and policy credibility. Colombia and Indonesia showed distinct tightening channels, while China’s reserve stock offered a partial regional cushion.

section_summaries.market_read: Cross assets confirm higher real discount rates rather than a conventional flight to safety.
section_summaries.next_check: Sustained oil relief is the key observable counterforce to restrictive policy pricing.
section_summaries.summary: Falling oil and flat breakevens contradicted an energy-driven Treasury selloff, while the stronger dollar, weaker gold, and a technology-led equity decline confirmed a real-rate shock. Calm shortest bills and successful financings kept the episode orderly despite severe volatility and crowded-position amplification.

section_summaries.market_read: The regime now hinges on confirmation across prices, auction demand, and global policy.
section_summaries.next_check: The first decisive check is May CPI at 08:30 ET on June 10, followed by PPI and claims.
section_summaries.summary: 3 tests will determine whether the bear flattening persists: US inflation and claims, Treasury supply absorption, and the global central-bank sequence. Broad price strength, weak coupon demand, or repeated tightening guidance would reinforce higher real and clearing rates; softer data and orderly auctions would reopen duration relief.
